program.spec_title: ISS Veggie seed film placement into plant pillows
warnings: No visible scale reference; object sizes and poses are estimates based on typical ISS hardware.

failure_classes.evidence: In orbit (0 g), the insert step released obj1 at s2.op1 with centre 0.7 mm above obj2's pocket rim (22.7 mm above pocket floor) while moving at 16.9 mm/s. The spec's target pose (36 mm from obj2 top) placed the packet above the pocket instead of inside it. The patch that lowered the final z to 13 mm (pocket floor) made both worlds pass, showing the spec's insertion target was wrong and pocket depth was missing.

In 0 g the rigid-body simulator has no friction or damping, so obj1 continued moving at 16.9 mm/s indefinitely after release above the rim. Increasing the wait_until timeout to 10 s did not help. A real robot in microgravity would experience contact damping and material friction.

reshoot.why: Interview gave only a horizontal clearance (10 mm). The pocket depth (vertical distance from rim to floor) is needed to define the correct insertion target.
reshoot.ask: What is the depth of the plant pillow pocket from rim to floor in millimetres?

reshoot.why: The video shows the astronaut placing the packet into the pocket but the exact final height relative to the pocket rim is not measurable from the clip.
reshoot.ask: Film a close-up side view of the packet being inserted into the pocket, showing how far the packet descends below the rim before release.

open_risks: Microgravity release may need active push or adhesion; the packet could rebound off the pocket floor and drift away.
Glove fingers may obstruct the packet during final placement, not modelled in the parallel gripper.
Packet orientation (symmetry none) may require alignment with pocket features not captured in the box shape.
ISS air currents or crew movement could disturb the unsecured packet after placement.
